  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The closed-without-merging clause rebases the branch but never names how to publish the rewritten branch, so a plain `git push` is rejected as non-fast-forward.
  WHY: The remote still holds the pre-rebase commits and CLAUDE.md §21.E allows `--force-with-lease` only after a §21.A reset, which this path skips, so the `[x]` steps are never published. All four reviewers rated this MAJOR; glm-5_3-flash also notes the clause never says to open a new draft PR.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:57-59 (template copy workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:64-66) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The rebase is instructed while the log edit is still an uncommitted working-tree change, and the text covers only the rebase-conflict abort.
  WHY: `git rebase` refuses a dirty tree, so the log update stays unpublished with no defined next step. Severity disagreement: sonnet-5_5 and minimax-m3 said NIT, gemini and glm said MAJOR; the highest is used.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:158 (template copy workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:169) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The Tool Access section declares Bash read-only while the Activation Log directs mutating git operations (checkout -B, fetch, rebase, merge --abort, push).
  WHY: A session may treat the two sections as conflicting capability boundaries and hand the commands to the operator, breaking the one-log-PR flow. minimax-m3 adds that the template Rules bullet at workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:50 still says "do not run ... git pushes yourself". sonnet-5_5 explicitly did not report this finding.

- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md (template copy workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md): "One log PR per session" bullet, closed-without-merging clause | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The rebase clause never says how to push the rewritten branch; the only push is a plain `git push`, and CLAUDE.md §21.E (lines 873-875) allows `--force-with-lease` only after a §21.A reset.
  WHY: The plain push is rejected as non-fast-forward, so the rebased `[x]` steps never reach the new draft PR. The suggested fix is to name `git push --force-with-lease origin <branch>` in both copies and add the phrase to the required strings in `tests/test_deploy_activate_command.py`.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md (template copy workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md): same clause; "Update after every step" and "One log PR per session" | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The rebase instruction is silent about a log edit that is still uncommitted.
  WHY: `git rebase` refuses to start on a dirty working tree, so the session has no defined next step. The fix is to commit the log update, then rebase.
- Tool Access / trust boundary: NONE. The reviewer reported nothing on this item.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template copy workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:66) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The clause rewrites the branch's history but never says how to publish it. The only push is a plain `git push` (line 58; line 166 in Rules). CLAUDE.md §21.E (CLAUDE.md:873-875) sanctions `--force-with-lease` only after a §21.A reset, §21.F (CLAUDE.md:885-903) scopes `-resend` to the push after a reset, and `tests/test_deploy_activate_command.py:216-238` has no required string for a publish command.
  WHY: The next `git push` is rejected non-fast-forward, so the rebased log commits never reach the remote and the confirmed `[x]` steps are lost, which is the loss the clause claims to prevent.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:57-59 (template copy workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:66) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The rebase is instructed while the just-confirmed log step is an unstaged working-tree change; the text handles only the conflict case.
  WHY: Git aborts with "cannot rebase: You have unstaged changes" before the rebase starts, so the update is never published and no next step is defined.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:158 (template copy workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:169) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Tool Access still declares Bash read-only while the Activation Log directs `git fetch`, `git rebase`, `git checkout -B`, `git merge --abort`, a push and a draft PR. The template Rules bullet (workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:50) still says "do not run the mutating deploy commands or git pushes yourself".
  WHY: A session may read the conflicting statements as the capability contract and hand the log-branch commands to the operator, breaking the one-log-PR-per-session automation. The writes themselves are correctly scoped, so the gap is declared-versus-effective.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:59 (template copy workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:66) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The rebase rewrites commits already pushed to the same-named remote branch, but the text never says how to publish the result. CLAUDE.md §21.E (.claude/docs/s21-merged-pr-commit-guard.md:164-166) sanctions `--force-with-lease` only after a §21.A reset, and the clause never says to open a new draft PR after the rebase.
  WHY: The plain `git push` is rejected non-fast-forward, so the `[x]` marks never publish and the session has no open PR to keep updating. The fix is to push with `git push --force-with-lease origin <branch>`, open one new draft PR, and add a matching test string in tests/test_deploy_activate_command.py:212-248.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:57-59 (template copy workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:64-66) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The PR-state check runs before the log commit, so the log edit is an unstaged change at rebase time, and the text covers only the rebase-conflict abort.
  WHY: `git rebase` refuses a dirty tree, so on every closed-PR log update the rebase aborts before doing anything and the update stays unpublished. The fix is to commit or stash the log edit before the fetch-and-rebase.
- .claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:158 (template copy workflow-templates/.claude/commands/deploy-activate.md:169) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Tool Access says Bash is read-only while the Activation Log directs mutating `git checkout -B`, `git fetch`, `git rebase` and `git merge --abort`.
  WHY: The conflicting capability boundaries could make a session stop and ask the operator for the branch surgery, breaking the automatic flow. The fix is to name this log-branch maintenance as bookkeeping in the Tool Access Bash bullet.
- Trust boundary and task completeness: NONE.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
